source.title: Input Swap Graphs: Discovering the role of neural network components at scale

record.tranche_reason: The post applies input-swap graphs and targeted interventions, rather than the original study's circuit-finding and evaluation procedure, to investigate IOI components and behavior.
record.gate_note: The post also discusses swap-graph theory and reports exploratory component analyses. Those are included only where the text states an outcome. Some graph and intervention results are presented only in linked plots or figures; no values are inferred from them.
record.test_reason: Uses input-swap graphs, a different patching-based method, to recover the roles of IOI heads in GPT-2 small (name movers, S-inhibition). It then looks for homologous head groups in GPT2-XL, Pythia-2.8B, GPT-Neo-2.7B and a Mistral 'battlestar' model, validated with targeted rewrites.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author concludes that swap graphs recover known IOI head roles in GPT-2 small, and found a new gender-encoding role (9.7 and battlestar 8.3). Larger models show surprisingly similar high-level mover and sender structure, validated by scrubbing and targeted rewrites. Rewrites are incomplete in large models, many components fit no candidate feature, and larger-model homologies are hypotheses.
record.recipe_differences: Uses input-swap graphs, Louvain communities, causal-scrubbing-style resampling, and targeted rewrites rather than reproducing the original circuit-finding and faithfulness/completeness/minimality procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports weaker head 9.9 clusters with logit difference than with KL divergence, a further loss of logit-difference clusters at a narrower Gaussian-kernel bandwidth, and non-monotonic resampling results that vary with partition method and entropy. It also reports different structure for particular prompt features and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Clusters from swap graphs give less destructive causal-scrubbing resampling than activation-vector clusters at high entropy, and about equal results at low entropy. The curves are non-monotonic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Patching-based input partitions preserve model function better than activation clustering.

fits_no_version.finding: MLP blocks have consistent communities, but these correlate only weakly with known IOI features and seem sensitive to the sentence ending.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLPs in the IOI task encode sentence-ending context rather than circuit variables.

record.problems: Many outcomes are shown in linked plots rather than stated numerically in the text. The post acknowledges imperfect swap-graph separation, context-related outliers, weak correspondence to candidate features in larger models, and incomplete targeted rewrites. Larger-model component correspondences are partly hypotheses rather than a full circuit analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No additional text-described result relevant to the listed versions was left out. Plots in linked external folders are not transcribed because their values are not present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: The full 26-head circuit and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No ablation of the main name movers and no test of backup takeover.
Training checkpoints, and reuse of components for other tasks.
Other circuit-discovery algorithms (e.g. ACDC) and ablation types for recovering the whole circuit.
No faithfulness or completeness evaluation of the IOI circuit under different ablations, metrics or distributions.
No test of IOI across templates, name orders or numbers of names. The dataset is restricted to 5 names (88 in one battlestar graph).

missing.what: A logit-difference swap graph of the S-inhibition head output is said to match the KL findings for heads further down. This bears on the metric-independence of role recovery.
missing.locator: Appendix: Swap graph with logit difference, last paragraph

record.verdict_notes: The study's swap-graph metric and kernel comparisons concern recovery of 9.9's role (V4), not the faithfulness evaluation of the circuit, so V5 links were removed. The V6 links were removed because ABB/BAB clustering shows the position signal, not cross-format robustness. The reader's V4 'challenges' label is replaced: the method still recovers the roles under KL divergence, and only the logit-difference variant fails. Author is a co-author of the IOI paper, but this post is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the complete 26-head, seven-class circuit or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria. It investigates selected GPT-2 small heads and reports swap-graph roles.
No ablation of main name movers followed by a test of whether backup heads take over.
Does not establish that the full circuit is the same across models, sizes or checkpoints, or test reuse of its components on other tasks. Roles in larger models are presented partly as hypotheses.
Compares swap-graph results using KL divergence and logit difference, but does not compare a broad range of circuit-finding methods or ablation types.
Does not comprehensively vary prompt distributions or reproduce the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality evaluation.
Does not establish IOI performance across all name orders, templates, or numbers of names. Several prompt-variant findings concern component-role clusters rather than behavioral performance.
